title: The Kind Lie
text:
The first story of Saadi's Gulistan tells of a king who ordered a prisoner to be put to death. Knowing he had nothing left to lose, the man began to curse the king in his own language, saying every abusive thing that came to him.

The king did not understand the words and asked his ministers what the prisoner was saying. One minister, a kind man, answered: "He is saying, 'Those who restrain their anger and forgive people are loved by God.'" The king was moved. He took pity on the prisoner and spared his life.

A second minister, a rival of the first, objected. "It is not right for men of our rank to speak anything but the truth in the king's presence," he said. "This man was cursing the king and insulting him."

The king frowned. "His lie pleases me more than the truth you have told," he said. "His was meant to do good, and yours was meant to do harm." Saadi adds the line for which the story is famous: a well meant falsehood is better than a truth that stirs up trouble.
lesson: Being right is not the only thing that matters in what you say. Ask whether your words will heal or harm before you speak them.
people: A king, a condemned prisoner, two ministers
source: Saadi, Gulistan (The Rose Garden), Chapter 1, Story 1
